title: When the Deadline Breaks
premise: Sable Thackeray, a whistle-blower who has survived by living under four names and taking cases no one will claim, is hired to verify a leaked voiceprint. The print unlocks a server in Geneva containing proof that a joint intelligence program called LATTICE has been assassinating witnesses across three governments — and Sable's own buried past is one of its case files. Hunted by an assassin who knows all four of his names, Sable must ally with a disgraced journalist and a defecting analyst to move the evidence through Vienna, Lisbon, and finally Washington before a treaty summit buries it forever. In the end Sable chooses truth over survival: he testifies under his real name, the one he swore he'd never speak again, knowing it may be the last thing he ever does.
about_author: Elodie Nakamura is a former investigative producer who spent a decade covering intelligence leaks before turning to fiction. She writes from a different city every year, a habit she describes as 'research for paranoia.'

chapters.title: Four Names, One Man
chapters.summary: Sable Thackeray, working under his fourth identity as a document broker in Rotterdam, takes an anonymous verification job. POV: Sable. The beat is quiet unease — competence masking loneliness, and the first hint that this job knows too much about him.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: The audio file matches a dead man's voice: Marcus Vale, an analyst who died two years ago. When Sable runs it against a Geneva server, it unlocks — addressed to him by his first name, the one no one living should know. POV: Sable. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Server Knows
chapters.summary: The server holds LATTICE files: sanctioned killings dressed as accidents, spanning three governments. One file is Sable himself — recruitment, betrayal, erasure. POV: Sable. Beat: vertigo; his identity was never his own.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Answers Dead Phones
chapters.summary: Sable contacts journalist Imara Osei, whose career was destroyed chasing Vale's death. She agrees to meet, testing him with questions only Vale could answer. POV: Imara. Beat: wary alliance between two people trained not to trust.

chapters.title: Contract on a Ghost
chapters.summary: In London, assassin Corvus receives four names and four faces — all of them Sable. His handler insists the target is already dead twice over. POV: Corvus. Beat: cold professionalism cracking into genuine intrigue at an impossible quarry.

chapters.title: Rotterdam Burns
chapters.summary: Sable's safehouse flat explodes minutes after he leaves. He realizes the leak came from inside the verification job itself — he was bait. POV: Sable. Beat: survival adrenaline curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Vienna Interlude
chapters.summary: Sable and Imara regroup in Vienna with analyst Nadia Brandt, a LATTICE defector carrying decryption keys. Nadia doesn't trust whistle-blowers; she's seen what they cost. POV: Nadia. Beat: friction, then grudging respect over a shared enemy.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Decrypted files reveal LATTICE answers to no single government — it sells deniability to all three. A treaty summit in ten days will formalize its immunity. POV: Nadia. Beat: horror at scale; the clock starts ticking audibly.

chapters.title: Corvus Closes
chapters.summary: Corvus tracks them to Vienna but hesitates when he recognizes the kill pattern — his own earlier contracts are in the files. He was building the machine he's now sent to protect. POV: Corvus. Beat: the first hairline fracture in loyalty.

chapters.title: The Safe House That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Their Vienna contact betrays them; a staged arrest becomes an ambush. Nadia is captured, the keys split between Sable and Imara. POV: Imara. Beat: guilt and resolve — she chose the story over the person, again.

chapters.title: Interrogation in the Dark
chapters.summary: Nadia endures questioning by a LATTICE liaison who offers her old life back. She gives up nothing true, but plants a false location. POV: Nadia. Beat: quiet heroism; power meets a will it can't purchase.

chapters.title: Lisbon, Off the Grid
chapters.summary: Sable and Imara go dark in Lisbon, using one of Sable's discarded identities as cover. Old debts surface: a fixer from his second life demands payment in favors. POV: Sable. Beat: the past as both shelter and trap.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name Speaks
chapters.summary: Imara discovers Sable's original identity — before the four aliases — and confronts him. He confesses what LATTICE made him do at twenty-three. POV: Imara. Beat: intimacy forged in confession; trust survives the truth.

chapters.title: Corvus Finds Religion
chapters.summary: Corvus intercepts the false location Nadia planted, realizes he's been played by his own side, and makes an uncharacteristic call: he contacts Sable. POV: Corvus. Beat: defection begins not from conscience but from insulted precision.

chapters.title: A Meeting of Assassins and Liars
chapters.summary: Sable, Imara, and Corvus meet in a shuttered fish cannery. Nobody trusts anybody; Corvus proves himself by naming the mole in their chain. POV: Sable. Beat: uneasy trinity — each holds a piece the others need.

chapters.title: Extraction of Nadia Brandt
chapters.summary: They spring Nadia from a black-site transit facility outside Porto. It works because Corvus uses his own credentials — burning his life behind him. POV: Corvus. Beat: the point of no return, crossed almost casually.

chapters.title: The Summit Gambit
chapters.summary: With 48 hours to the treaty signing, the team plans to inject the files into the summit's secure briefing system — requiring someone inside. Imara's old editor still has press accreditation. POV: Imara. Beat: hope sharpening into a plan with too many teeth.

chapters.title: Everything Breaks at Once
chapters.summary: The mole resurfaces; the plan leaks; Corvus's handler sends a kill team to the hotel. Nadia is wounded covering the escape, and the keys nearly fall into LATTICE hands. POV: Nadia. Beat: catastrophe — the plan survives by a thread and blood.

chapters.title: Washington, D.C., Day Zero
chapters.summary: Summit day. While Imara triggers the file injection, Sable walks into the plenary hall uninvited, using his real name at security — the only credential that can't be dismissed. POV: Sable. Beat: terror transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Sable stands before delegates and names LATTICE, its victims, and himself, while the injected files cascade onto official screens. Delegations fracture; the treaty stalls. Corvus eliminates the liaison sent to silence the room. POV: alternating Sable/Imara. Beat: climax — truth spoken aloud cannot be re-swallowed.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Hearings begin; three governments scramble to disown what they funded. Sable, publicly alive and publicly named, can never vanish again. Corvus disappears into the machinery he betrayed. POV: Imara. Beat: bittersweet victory; exposure as both freedom and sentence.

chapters.title: One Name Is Enough
chapters.summary: Months later, Sable lives openly under his birth name, working with Imara on the next story. A postcard arrives with no signature — only a voiceprint waveform. He smiles, and files it away. POV: Sable. Beat: resolution with a pulse — the war continues, but he's no longer hiding.
